chapter: Blue Devils, Moten and the Reno Club
title: How he became 'Count' Basie on a Kansas City broadcast
summary: Basie confirms the announcer's quote about Earl Hines and Duke Ellington and calling him Count, but says it was another Kansas City spot, not the Reno Club.

story.theme_name: How I got my name: nicknames and band monikers
story.community_name: How I got my name: nicknames and band names

blocks.x: "Contrary to several conflicting stories, I got the name Count right in Kansas City in 1936 while at the Reno Club."
"I was known as Bill Basie at that time. One night while we were broadcasting, the announcer called me to the microphone for those usual few words of introduction." Did you say this?

"He commented that Bill Basie was a rather ordinary name and further, that there were a couple of well-known bandleaders named Earl Hines and Duke Ellington." You're laughing, right? "Then he said, 'Bill, I think I'll call you Count Basie from now on. Is that all right with you?' I thought he was kidding, shrugged my shoulders and replied, 'Okay.' Well, that was the last time I was ever introduced as Bill Basie. From then on, it was Count Basie and I never did lose that nickname. It's funny the way those things will stick.

I always get a big kick when an announcer or interviewer will ask, 'Count, tell us how you got that royal title, will you?' That's usually the first question and by now, I can reel off the answer to that one without catching my breath." Is that true?
Was it true that he one night at the Reno club asked you?
Do you remember who it was, the announcer?
And he said to you that there are a lot of royal titles like Earl Hines and Duke Ellington. Did he say that?
And he said, 'I think I'll call you Count Basie.' He said that?
The Reno Club? You were not broadcasting from the Reno Club?
Yeah, right, but some other club?
The quotes are right. You mean, it was another club in Kansas City?
But you're not going to tell me.
Yeah, all right. I'm sure you do.
